newsitem.title: ISRAEL: CPC completes purchase of Israel Edible.
newsitem.headline: CPC completes purchase of Israel Edible.

text.p: America's CPC International has completed the purchase of Koor Industries' 24.5 percent holding in Israel Edible Products, Koor said on Tuesday.
Koor said CPC paid $37.5 million for the holding in Israel Edible, which is also known as Tami. The acquisition brings the American company's total stake in Israeli Edible to about 84 percent.
"The sale is part of Koor's strategy to concentrate in the companies that we see as our core business and to pull out of the others," Koor CEO Benjamin Gaon said in a statement.

CPC acquired a 51 percent holding in Israel Edible in 1991 for $43 million and then helped introduce CPC products, like Hellman's mayonnaise, to the line. CPC brands now make up 12-15 percent of Israel Edible's product line, the company said.

Israel Edible produces 90 percent of Israel's margarine as well as soups, sauces, breakfast cereals, snacks and chocolates. The company said sales last year were $250 million, making it Israel's third-largest dry groceries producer.

Koor, Israel's largest holding company, is focusing on telecommunications, electronics, agrochemicals, building materials and energy distribution. It retains smaller holdings in food, most notably Shemen Industries.

Richard Oppenheim, Tami's managing director, told Reuters that the acquisition would not lead to any fundamental change in the company's strategy. "Effectively CPC had management control under the terms of the original (purchase) agreement," he said.

Oppenheim said CPC was looking tentatively at the possibility of using Israel Edible as a Middle East base. "Many of the (Israel Edible) products are not relevant because of the low purchasing power in the region," he noted.
Israel Edible, however, has been supplying technical known-how to a CPC-controlled joint venture in Jordan called Best Foods, he said.
The sale to CPC marks the further penetration of multinational food companies into Israel's food industry. Last July, Nestle SA acquired 40 percent of Osem Investments over 1996.
Unilever took a 50 percent stake in closely held Strauss Dairies' ice cream business in September 1995 and France's Danone 20 percent in Strauss' other dairy business this month.
